text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- German police exclude possibility of accomplices in Monday's Air Malta hijack which ended in Cologne where two Turks gave themselves up after demanding the release of Mehmed Ali Agca, the Turk who shot Pope John Paul in 1981. Another two passengers on the flight to Istanbul had been under questioning after suspicion that they were accomplices.

- Tourism Minister Karmenu Vella tells hoteliers Malta could remain competitive if prices are kept in check, and he was optimistic tourism arrivals would grow this year after falling in the past two years.

- Carlo Cini, president of Association of General Retailers and Traders (GRTU), resigns from Nationalist Party after 40 years as member. He accused the party, now in opposition, of seeking political advantage from the government's plan to introduce a new system of indirect taxation. Opposition leader Eddie Fenech Adami replied that the party always sought the national interest, even if the new tax system could favour a few GRTU members.
- Four seriously injured in two traffic accidents.

- Asco Security, a small private firm, claims discrimination in award of contract for security services at state-owned Public Broadcasting Services. Prime Minister Alfred Sant told parliament the contract, which went to another firm, was awarded after a call for tenders.
